newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Philips Taiwan to invest T$4 bln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Philips Taiwan to invest T$4 bln in 1997.

text.p: Philips Taiwan, a wholly owned unit of Dutch giant Philips Electronics NV, said on Tuesday it would invest T$4 billion in local operations in 1997 and make Taiwan its personal computer headquarters.

"Asia Pacific region is a rapidly growing area. To keep up with the growth, we plan to invest T$4 billion to upgrade our operations and expand our production lines in Taiwan during 1997," company spokeswoman Denise Sun said by telephone.
The investment would concentrate on semiconductors, personal computers and consumer electronic products, Sun said.
Sun said the company's revenues would surpass T$100 billion in 1996, up from 1995's T$93.2 billion.
"To show our commitment, the company also has decided to turn Taiwan into the headquarters for its personal computer business," Sun said.
Philips Electronics transferred its computer monitor unit headquarters to Taiwan from the Netherlands in January.
"It is no surprise that we choose Taiwan as headquarters for monitors and PCs because Taiwan is already a kingdom of computers," Sun said.
